description: This preprint addresses how growing data centre demand reshapes power system dynamics while offering fast, controllable flexibility. It proposes a data-driven linearisation framework based on decision-tree constraint learning to embed nonlinear nadir frequency constraints into a mixed-integer linear programme for frequency-secured unit commitment, so that generation schedules and data centre fast frequency response can be optimised together. Case studies on a benchmark system and a 2030 scenario with higher data centre penetration show that a larger share of flexible data centre load consistently improves cost efficiency and supports renewable integration, with diminishing marginal returns, which motivates the Marginal Flexibility Value metric for the economic value of extra flexibility. Producer: Ren, Sun, Wang and Harrison, submitted 1 October 2025. Coverage: benchmark power systems, not a specific grid. Access: free arXiv preprint; only the abstract page was read, and code or data availability was not confirmed. Licence and cost: free to read; licence arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence (the paper; no open reuse licence). Caveats: the results are for a benchmark and a hypothetical 2030 scenario. Simulation uses: the framework supports optimisation of power system operation with flexible data centre loads and planning of frequency support. Related record: the AI data centre flexibility grid capacity expansion model (model-ai-data-centre-flexibility-grid-capacity-expansion-defer-shift).
